issues.description: test_sign_message_by_address never asserts the verification succeeded
issues.detail: The new test calls `verify_signature` but discards the result. `verify_signature` returns a VerifySignatureResponse with `isValid=False` and an error string instead of raising on bad signatures, so this test would silently pass even if signing/verification regressed. Add `assert (await ...).isValid is True`.

issues.description: Module-level `signing_mode_enum` function shadows property of same name on request dataclasses
issues.detail: `wallet_request_types.py` defines a free function `signing_mode_enum(request)` and also adds a property named `signing_mode_enum` on both SignMessageByAddress and SignMessageByID that calls it. This naming collision is confusing, breaks `from ... import signing_mode_enum` ergonomics, and risks future bugs if anyone reorders or renames. Rename the helper (e.g. `_compute_signing_mode`) or inline it.

issues.description: `verify_signature` docstring still references a `request` parameter that no longer exists
issues.detail: The function was extracted from the RPC method and now takes individual keyword args, but the docstring left over from the move says `:param request:` / `:return:`. This is misleading for callers reading the new util's API. Replace with a real param description.

issues.description: `convert_secret_key_to_synthetic` is an instance method on Wallet but uses no instance state
issues.detail: It's defined on `Wallet` and then always invoked through `main_wallet.convert_secret_key_to_synthetic(...)` even when signing for DID/NFT wallets. It has no `self` dependency. Make it a `@staticmethod` (or move to `signing.py` next to `sign_message`) so callers don't reach across an unrelated wallet instance just to derive a key.

issues.description: Layering inversion: `chia/wallet/util/signing.py` imports VerifySignatureResponse from wallet_request_types
issues.detail: A low-level util now depends on the request-types module, while RPC code imports the util. If wallet_request_types ever needs anything from signing util (or vice versa), this creates a circular import risk. Consider moving VerifySignatureResponse into the util or keeping the util pure and constructing the response in the RPC layer.

issues.description: DIDWallet error message wording silently changed
issues.detail: Original raised `"Invalid inner DID puzzle."`, new `current_p2_puzzle_hash` raises `"Invalid DID inner puzzle."`. Likely cosmetic, but any external tooling/log scraping that grepped for the old string will break. Either restore the original wording or call it out in the changelog.

review.summary: The refactor is a clean lift-and-shift of signing/verification into a shared util and preserves behavior for the common path, but a few rough edges remain. The new `test_sign_message_by_address` doesn't assert `isValid`, so it can't catch verification regressions. There's a naming collision between the module-level `signing_mode_enum` helper and the property of the same name on the request dataclasses. The util keeps a stale `:param request:` docstring after extraction, and `convert_secret_key_to_synthetic` is awkwardly placed as an instance method on Wallet despite being used for DID/NFT signing through `main_wallet`. None are blocking, but the test gap and the naming shadowing are worth fixing before merge.
